title: Ledger Configuration
description: Optional ledger.yaml in the config home. dsn present: the Ledger database is the authority for disposition layers and layer files are read-only snapshots of it; dsn absent: layer files are the ledger. signing and identity apply in both modes. No environment-variable overrides. Secrets (keypair password, identity tokens, the caller's ledger token) never belong here.

dsn.description: SQLAlchemy URL of the Ledger database, passed unchanged to the Ledger client: postgresql+psycopg://… (PostgreSQL via psycopg 3) or sqlite:////absolute/path/ledger.db. The Ledger requires traust_storage in the same database, so this is usually the storage database under the ledger's own role. This value may contain credentials; do not log it.

signing.description: How layer Merkle roots are signed.

required.description: Refuse to write an unsigned layer.

method.description: keypair: a cosign private key; identity: keyless Sigstore/OIDC.

key_path.description: Absolute path of the cosign private key (keypair). Its password comes from the runner's COSIGN_PASSWORD, never this file.

identity.description: How the Ledger verifies the caller's token. The token itself is the caller's credential (ledger auth login or a workload token file).

directory_command.description: Employee-directory cross-check command run for each actor.
